extracted.intended_audience: journalists and consumers of health care news (and PR/marketing)
extracted.subtask_short: evaluating health news and PR releases
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and organizational policies for reviewing and rating health care journalism, advertising, marketing, and public relations messages to help consumers and journalists critically analyze health care claims. Emphasizes independence, disclosure, accuracy, balance, completeness, and use of an explicit rating/"star" system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy, balance, and completeness of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide accurate, balanced and complete information about the tradeoffs involved in health care decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mission is to improve public dialogue by promoting principles of shared decision-making reinforced by accurate, balanced and complete information about tradeoffs. Reviews are intended to help consumers critically analyze claims about health care interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of shared decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Content should promote the principles of shared decision-making when presenting health care options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HealthNewsReview.org emphasizes shared decision-making as a goal of better public information about health care interventions; reviews look for material that supports understanding of benefits and harms so consumers and clinicians can make informed choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from industry influence (no advertising/funding conflicts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept advertising or funding from entities whose support would represent a conflict of interest; ensure content has not been influenced by commercial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site does not accept advertising nor funding from any entity whose support would represent a conflict of interest. This is intended so readers know content has not been influenced — directly or indirectly — by any commercial interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: No editorial control by funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders must not have editorial control over the operation or content of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the project has accepted grants (e.g., Laura and John Arnold Foundation; Informed Medical Decisions Foundation), the site states: 'No funder has ever had, nor will they ever have, any editorial control over the operation of the project.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of industry-independent experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit and use experts who do not accept payments from drug or device companies or other commercial entities whose support might represent a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All expert contributors pledge they do not accept payments from drug or device companies or from any commercial entity whose support might represent a conflict of interest. The site also hosts a list of industry-independent health care experts for journalists to quote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of financial interests for quoted experts
rubrics_metrics.description: When quoting non-team experts, ask about any financial interests they may have in the topic and disclose those interests in the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an outside expert is quoted, HealthNewsReview.org will ask about financial interests and will disclose those interests in the article to preserve transparency and help readers assess potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limits and non-advocacy stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not provide medical advice or serve as an advocacy group; limit scope according to staff capacity and mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site explicitly states it is not equipped to host a definitive forum on medical science, does not give medical advice, and is not an advocacy group. It explains practical limits (small editorial staff, budget) and that it cannot review every story or promotional message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of varied message types (journalism, advertising, PR, marketing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply review criteria across health care journalism, advertising, marketing, public relations and other messages that may influence consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HealthNewsReview.org evaluates journalism and promotional messages and provides criteria that consumers can use to evaluate these messages themselves; improving quality and flow of health care information is seen as contributing to health care reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an explicit star-score rating system
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate stories using a 'star' score determined by the site's methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site references 'How the “star score” is determined' and 'How we rate stories' as part of its evaluation approach (the About page lists these pages but does not reproduce the scoring details here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about funding and acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose sources of funding and acknowledge supporters while maintaining editorial independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site lists its past and current funders (e.g., Laura and John Arnold Foundation; Informed Medical Decisions Foundation) and thanks donors, while reiterating no funder has editorial control. Donations are solicited via a 'GIVE NOW' button and are disclosed to readers.
